findings.message: Resolved (verified): review-7-qa's finding on the 'blink-code' clue (engine-trace). The clue description in story.r10.json (lines 66-68) now reads "The little box blinked and thudded twice, slow and quick, like a secret code." with no causal claim about Ivy's call-out, matching the passage's own unconditional narration (line 381, "Then it gave a soft thud, twice, like a secret code.") that occurs before either choice. Diffing story.r9.json against story.r10.json confirms only this description string, the 'call-out' choice label, and the version number changed on this passage; requires/target/effects are untouched.

Resolved (verified): review-7-qa's finding that the 'chalk-note' item and 'blink-code' clue were dead ends with no later payoff (unlike hook-pole/late-log, which gate 'open-careful' and are named again in climax-careful). Narrative-designer determined a genuine narrative callback is not possible without restructuring the graph (both choices converge to the same next passage before any branch-specific text exists, so there is no later point that can distinguish a reader who took the branch from one who did not), and instead removed the implied future payoff from the surrounding text: nib-ask's unconditional line ("Nib snapped off a small chalk note. It lay there, like a tiny gift.") and the 'promise-nib' choice label (now "Pick up the small chalk note to keep") no longer frame the note as a kept promise, and the 'call-out' label no longer implies an answer is coming. This was one of the two resolutions review-7-qa itself proposed as acceptable (reword to pure atmosphere) and I confirm it was applied consistently: grep across the full r10 draft for 'promise', 'chalk-note', 'blink-code' and 'secret code' shows no remaining promise/payoff framing attached to either collectible. The items/clues remain mechanically inert (no requires block references them, confirmed by the unchanged graph report), which is by design and was already assessed as not a soft-lock risk.
